category_title: Pupils with high SNA dependence and learned helplessness
minimal_context: The student is participating in a group circle time activity and is asked to share an answer with the class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is your turn to share in circle time. What was your favorite part of the story?

STUDENT: (Stays quiet, looking down) Um...

TUTOR: Do you remember what happened at the end?

STUDENT: I know, I'm trying to think...

TUTOR: You liked the part with the dog. Just tell everyone you liked the dog.

STUDENT: Like we do a circle time and I’m just trying to think of the answers . . . and you tell me it!

options.A: Employ a visual or gestural prompt to help the student answer during circle time.
options.B: Send a clear message to the student regarding dissatisfaction with their behavior during circle time.
options.C: Keep a kit comprising assorted coloring sheets and crayons ready during circle time.
options.D: Alter the original circle time plans to incorporate the student's specific story contributions.
